issue_context.title: Feature: Open Windows Terminal as admin using ctrl + shift + `
issue_context.body:
### What feature or improvement do you think would benefit Files?

On Windows 10, on MS File Explorer (MSFE) you can open a shell terminal by using the combo ALT->F->S->(A|R) A for Admin or R for Regular User.  
This is **extremely** handy as one can open a shell as admin on the path we want to work with with ease, especially for software installation etc.  

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/90066435/218550668-d1cad969-4e6d-4d55-a605-13f922790ba8.png)


On Windows 11, the brilliant minds of Microsoft removed any of the ALT keys from MSFE, because reasons.  

I've started using Files, I like the way it works, and having this feature would be great. 

### Requirements

- This proposal will require the addition of a hot-key or sequence of keys that would open a (power)shell terminal on the current location as administrator. 


### Files Version

2.4.33.0

### Windows Version

Win 10 - 10.0.19044.2486

### Comments

_No response_
